name: ۱۱۰۰ کلمه‌ای که باید بدانید
description: کلمات کتاب 1100 Words You Need to Know (Barron's) با تعریف، مثال، مترادف و توضیحات کامل

words.coreMeaning: کوتاه کردن یک متن بدون از دست دادن معنای اصلی
definitions: To shorten a text without losing the essential meaning.
To condense or reduce in scope.
examples: The editor decided to abridge the novel for younger readers.
His rights were abridged by the new regulations.
words.trap: با 'a bridge' (پل) اشتباه نگیرید؛ ریشه لاتین abbreviare است

words.coreMeaning: توانایی درک سریع و تصمیم‌گیری درست
definitions: Keen insight and good judgment.
The ability to make good decisions and judgments in a particular subject or business.
examples: Her business acumen helped the company grow rapidly.
He lacked the political acumen needed to succeed in office.
words.trap: با 'acme' (اوج) اشتباه نگیرید؛ تلفظ: اَکیومن

words.coreMeaning: بسیار ماهر و باتجربه در کاری
definitions: Highly skilled or proficient at something.
Having a thorough knowledge of something.
examples: She is adept at solving complex mathematical problems.
He became adept at navigating office politics.
words.trap: هم صفت و هم اسم است؛ با 'adapt' (سازگار کردن) اشتباه نگیرید

words.coreMeaning: مهربان و خوش‌رو در رفتار با دیگران
definitions: Friendly, good-natured, and easy to talk to.
Pleasant and at ease in talking to others.
examples: The affable host made everyone feel welcome at the party.
Despite his high position, the manager remained affable and approachable.
words.trap: با 'effable' (قابل بیان) و 'ineffable' (غیرقابل بیان) اشتباه نگیرید

words.coreMeaning: بدون دشمنی و با حسن نیت
definitions: Having a spirit of friendliness; without serious disagreement or rancour.
Done in a peaceful and cooperative way.
examples: They reached an amicable settlement outside of court.
The divorce was amicable, with both parties agreeing on terms.
words.trap: با 'amicable' و 'amiable' فرق دارد: amicable برای روابط، amiable برای شخصیت

words.coreMeaning: بسیار مشتاق و پرحرارت
definitions: Enthusiastic or passionate.
Burning; glowing.
examples: He was an ardent supporter of environmental conservation.
She expressed her ardent desire to pursue higher education.
words.trap: با 'ardour/ardor' (شور و حرارت) از همین خانواده است

words.coreMeaning: جرأت‌مند و بی‌پروا
definitions: Showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks.
Extremely bold or daring.
examples: The audacious plan to climb Everest in winter shocked the mountaineering community.
Her audacious decision to quit her job and start a business paid off.
words.trap: با 'audible' (شنیدنی) اشتباه نگیرید؛ معنای منفی هم می‌تواند داشته باشد (گستاخ)

words.coreMeaning: حرص شدید به پول و ثروت
definitions: Extreme greed for wealth or material gain.
An excessive or insatiable desire for money or riches.
examples: His avarice led him to exploit workers for profit.
The king's avarice knew no bounds as he taxed the poor mercilessly.
words.trap: با 'avid' (مشتاق) فرق دارد؛ avarice همیشه بار منفی دارد

words.coreMeaning: فاقد اصالت و تازگی، تکراری
definitions: So lacking in originality as to be obvious and boring.
Commonplace; unoriginal.
examples: The movie's plot was banal and predictable.
She refused to make banal conversation at the dinner party.
words.trap: با 'canal' (کانال) از نظر تلفظ اشتباه نگیرید؛ تلفظ: بِنال

words.coreMeaning: خواهان خوبی و رفاه دیگران
definitions: Well-meaning and kindly.
Charitable; generous in giving.
examples: The benevolent donor funded the construction of a new hospital.
She gave him a benevolent smile as he stumbled through his speech.
words.trap: با 'malevolent' (بدخواه) متضاد است؛ هر دو از 'volent' (خواستن)

words.coreMeaning: عامل نابودی یا خرابی
definitions: A thing that spoils or damages something.
A plant disease, especially one caused by fungi.
To have a severely detrimental effect on.
examples: Poverty is a blight on modern society.
The potato blight destroyed the entire harvest.
The scandal blighted his political career.
words.trap: هم اسم و هم فعل است؛ در معماری 'urban blight' (فرسودگی شهری) کاربرد زیادی دارد

words.coreMeaning: استفاده از کلمات بزرگ و پرطمطراق بدون معنای واقعی
definitions: High-sounding but with little meaning; inflated.
Using impressive-sounding words but having little meaning.
examples: The politician's bombastic speech failed to impress the educated audience.
His bombastic writing style was full of grandiose but empty phrases.
words.trap: از 'bomb' (بمب) نیامده؛ از 'bombast' (پنبه زیر لباس، حرف پوچ)

words.coreMeaning: توانایی شناور ماندن یا روحیه شاد
definitions: Able to float or keep things floating.
Cheerful and optimistic.
Showing the ability to recover quickly from setbacks.
examples: The buoyant economy encouraged new investments.
Her buoyant personality lifted everyone's spirits.
Cork is a naturally buoyant material.
words.trap: u خاموش است: تلفظ: بوی‌اَنت؛ از 'buoy' (شناور)

words.coreMeaning: ترکیبی از صداهای ناهنجار و گوش‌خراش
definitions: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
An unpleasant mixture of loud sounds.
examples: The cacophony of car horns filled the busy intersection.
The cacophony of the construction site made it impossible to concentrate.
words.trap: از یونانی kakos (بد) + phone (صدا)؛ متضاد: euphony (آهنگ خوش)

words.coreMeaning: تغییر ناگهانی و غیرقابل پیش‌بینی در رفتار یا تصمیمات
definitions: Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behaviour.
Fickle; unpredictable.
examples: The capricious weather in spring makes it hard to plan outdoor events.
Her capricious nature made it difficult for employees to know where they stood.
words.trap: با 'caprice' (هوسرانی) از همین خانواده؛ از ایتالیایی capriccio

words.coreMeaning: عاملی که باعث تسریع یا آغاز تغییر می‌شود
definitions: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction.
A person or thing that precipitates an event or change.
examples: The assassination was the catalyst for the revolution.
She acted as a catalyst for change within the organization.
words.trap: با 'analyst' (تحلیلگر) اشتباه نگیرید؛ در شیمی و جامعه‌شناسی کاربرد دارد

words.coreMeaning: نرمش و مهربانی در برخورد با مجرمان
definitions: Mercy; lenience.
An act of mercy or leniency by a person in authority.
examples: The governor granted clemency to the wrongly convicted man.
The prisoner appealed to the king for clemency.
words.trap: متضاد 'inclement' (سخت، نامساعد) در مورد آب‌وهوای بد استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: آنقدر قوی که توجه را جلب یا اجبار کند
definitions: Evoking interest or attention in a powerfully irresistible way.
Forceful and convincing.
examples: The lawyer presented a compelling argument for her client's innocence.
The documentary tells a compelling story of survival.
words.trap: هم برای چیزهای جذاب و هم برای استدلال قوی استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: تلاش برای آشتی و کاهش تنش
definitions: Intended or likely to placate or pacify.
Making or willing to make concessions to restore good relations.
examples: His conciliatory tone helped resolve the dispute between the two departments.
She offered a conciliatory handshake after the heated argument.
words.trap: با 'reconciliatory' مرتبط است اما conciliatory بیشتر در انگلیسی رایج است

words.coreMeaning: مسئله‌ای بسیار دشوار و گیج‌کننده
definitions: A confusing and difficult problem or question.
A paradox or dilemma that is difficult to resolve.
examples: The ethical conundrum of AI decision-making concerns many researchers.
Finding a balance between work and life remains a conundrum for many.
words.trap: جمع ندارد (usually singular)؛ ریشه نامشخص است

words.coreMeaning: مقدار زیاد و بیش از حد معمول
definitions: Abundant in supply or quantity.
Large in quantity; plentiful.
examples: She took copious notes during the lecture.
The region receives copious rainfall during the monsoon season.
words.trap: با 'copier' (کپی‌کننده) اشتباه نگیرید؛ بیشتر برای مقدار استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: نداشتن مقدار کافی از چیزی
definitions: A scarcity or lack of something.
An insufficient quantity or supply.
examples: There is a dearth of qualified teachers in rural areas.
The dearth of evidence made the case difficult to prosecute.
words.trap: با 'death' (مرگ) اشتباه نگیرید! تلفظ متفاوت است

words.coreMeaning: دیگر فعال یا موجود نبودن
definitions: No longer existing or functioning.
Expired; dead.
examples: The company became defunct after filing for bankruptcy.
That organization has been defunct for over a decade.
words.trap: از لاتین defunctus (مرده)؛ برای شرکت‌ها و سازمان‌های تعطیل‌شده زیاد استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: تأثیر بد و مضر داشتن
definitions: Causing harm or damage.
Harmful; having a harmful effect.
examples: Smoking has deleterious effects on lung health.
The deleterious impact of pollution on marine life is well documented.
words.trap: با 'delete' (حذف) ارتباط معنایی ندارد؛ ریشه یونانی دارد

words.coreMeaning: توصیف دقیق یا ترسیم مرزها
definitions: To describe or portray something precisely.
To indicate the exact position of a border or boundary.
examples: The report delineates the responsibilities of each department.
The fence delineates the boundary between the two properties.
words.trap: با 'decline' (کاهش) و 'deviate' (انحراف) اشتباه نگیرید

words.coreMeaning: فن ایراد سخنرانی واضح و مؤثر
definitions: The skill of clear and expressive speech, especially of distinct pronunciation and articulation.
The art of effective public speaking.
examples: She took elocution lessons to improve her public speaking.
His polished elocution impressed everyone at the conference.
words.trap: با 'eloquence' فرق دارد: elocution بیشتر درباره تلفظ و ادا، eloquence درباره بلاغت محتوا

words.coreMeaning: توانایی بیان مؤثر و جذاب
definitions: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.
Clearly expressing or indicating something.
examples: She gave an eloquent speech about the importance of education.
His silence was an eloquent testimony to his guilt.
words.trap: با 'elocution' فرق دارد؛ eloquence بیشتر درباره قدرت بیان و معناست

words.coreMeaning: شروع یک کار جدید یا سوار بر کشتی شدن
definitions: To board a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.
To begin a new course of action.
examples: She embarked on a new career in data science.
The passengers embarked on the cruise ship at noon.
words.trap: معمولاً با 'on' یا 'upon' می‌آید: embark on something

words.coreMeaning: تقلید با هدف برابری یا برتری
definitions: To try to equal or surpass, typically by imitation.
To match or surpass, usually by imitation.
examples: Young athletes often emulate their sporting heroes.
The company tried to emulate the success of its competitors.
words.trap: با 'imitate' فرق دارد: emulate شامل تحسین و تلاش برای برابری است

words.coreMeaning: چیزی یا کسی که درک آن دشوار است
definitions: A person or thing that is mysterious or difficult to understand.
A puzzling or inexplicable occurrence.
examples: The disappearance of the plane remains an enigma.
She was an enigma to her colleagues — quiet yet incredibly effective.
words.trap: جمع: enigmas؛ با 'enigmatic' (رمزآلود) از همین خانواده

words.coreMeaning: ماندگاری بسیار کوتاه
definitions: Lasting for a very short time.
Transient; fleeting.
examples: Social media fame is often ephemeral.
The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms attracts millions of visitors.
words.trap: از یونانی ephemeros (یک‌روزه)؛ با 'eternal' (ابدی) متضاد است

words.coreMeaning: دارای چند معنی یا مبهم
definitions: Open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous.
Uncertain or questionable in meaning.
examples: The politician gave an equivocal response to the reporter's question.
The results of the study were equivocal and required further research.
words.trap: با 'unequivocal' (صریح) متضاد است؛ equivocate یعنی طفره رفتن

words.coreMeaning: دارای احساسات عمیق و شدید
definitions: Having or displaying a passionate intensity.
Warm; burning; hot.
examples: She is a fervent advocate for children's rights.
The fervent crowd cheered for their team.
words.trap: با 'fervor' (شور و حرارت) از همین خانواده؛ تلفظ: فِروِنت

words.coreMeaning: دارای رنگ قرمز یا زبان پرآرایش
definitions: Having a red or flushed complexion.
Excessively ornate or flowery in style.
examples: His florid complexion suggested he enjoyed good food and wine.
The author's florid prose was criticized as overwrought.
words.trap: از لاتین flos (گل)؛ دو معنای متفاوت: رنگ قرمز و سبک پرآرایش

words.coreMeaning: رخ دادن بر اساس شانس و تصادف
definitions: Happening by accident or chance rather than design.
Lucky; fortunate.
examples: A fortuitous meeting at the airport led to a business partnership.
The discovery of penicillin was a fortuitous accident.
words.trap: سنتاً فقط به معنای 'تصادفی' است نه 'خوش‌شانس'؛ اما در محاصره مدرن به هر دو معنا استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: پرهیز از هدر دادن پول یا منابع
definitions: Sparing or economical with regard to money or food.
Thrifty; not wasteful.
examples: Her frugal habits allowed her to save enough for a down payment.
He lived a frugal life, never spending money on luxuries.
words.trap: با 'miserly' (خسیس) فرق دارد: frugal بار مثبت، miserly بار منفی دارد

words.coreMeaning: انجام کاری به صورت مخفیانه و با ترس
definitions: Attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt or a belief that discovery would lead to trouble.
Secretive; sneaky.
examples: He cast a furtive glance at his phone during the meeting.
The furtive exchange of money raised suspicions.
words.trap: از لاتین furtivus (دزدیده)؛ معمولاً بار منفی دارد

words.coreMeaning: تحریک کسی به اقدام فوری
definitions: To shock or excite someone into taking action.
To coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc.
examples: The crisis galvanized the community into action.
Her speech galvanized voters to head to the polls.
words.trap: دو معنا دارد: 1) تحریک 2) پوشش فلزی با روی؛ از نام دانشمند Luigi Galvani

words.coreMeaning: بدون دلیل یا بدون پرداخت
definitions: Uncalled for; lacking good reason; unwarranted.
Given or done free of charge.
examples: The movie was criticized for its gratuitous violence.
His gratuitous insult offended everyone in the room.
words.trap: با 'gratitude' (قدردانی) ریشه مشترک دارد اما معنا متفاوت است

words.coreMeaning: فاقد شانس و خوشبختی
definitions: Unfortunate; having no luck.
Luckless.
examples: The hapless tourist lost his wallet on the first day of vacation.
The hapless team lost every game that season.
words.trap: از 'hap' (شانس) + 'less' (بدون)؛ نه از 'happy'

words.coreMeaning: بسیار مهم و ضروری، یا دستور
definitions: Of vital importance; crucial.
Giving an authoritative command; peremptory.
A verb form expressing a command.
examples: It is imperative that we act quickly to address climate change.
The imperative to reduce costs drove the company's decision.
'Sit down!' is an imperative sentence.
words.trap: هم صفت و هم اسم؛ در دستور زبان 'imperative mood' حالت امری است

words.coreMeaning: عدم نفوذ یا عدم تأثیرپذیری
definitions: Not allowing fluid to pass through.
Unable to be affected by something.
examples: The material is impervious to water and stains.
She seemed impervious to criticism from her colleagues.
words.trap: معمولاً با 'to' می‌آید: impervious to something

words.coreMeaning: بدون قصد و ناخواسته
definitions: Not resulting from or achieved through deliberate planning.
Unintentional; accidental.
examples: His inadvertent remark caused a misunderstanding.
The inadvertent deletion of the file was a costly mistake.
words.trap: با 'inadvisable' (ناصواب) اشتباه نگیرید؛ از in + advert (توجه)

words.coreMeaning: دارای قدرت تحلیل و نفوذ ذهنی
definitions: Intelligently analytical and clear-thinking.
Sharp; penetrating.
examples: Her incisive analysis of the financial report impressed the board.
The journalist asked incisive questions that the politician struggled to answer.
words.trap: از لاتین incidere (برش دادن)؛ مثبت و ستایش‌آمیز است

words.coreMeaning: بی‌توجهی و نداشتن علاقه
definitions: Having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned.
Neither good nor bad; mediocre.
examples: She was indifferent to the outcome of the election.
His indifferent performance disappointed the coach.
words.trap: با 'different' (متفاوت) اشتباه نگیرید؛ indifferent یعنی بی‌تفاوت

words.coreMeaning: تمایل به اجتناب از فعالیت و کار
definitions: Wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy.
Causing little or no pain.
examples: His indolent lifestyle eventually led to health problems.
The indolent pace of reform frustrated reformers.
words.trap: با 'insolent' (گستاخ) اشتباه نگیرید؛ معانی کاملاً متفاوت

words.coreMeaning: پنهانی در حال گسترش و آسیب‌رسانی
definitions: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.
Treacherous; crafty.
examples: The insidious spread of misinformation threatens democracy.
Cancer is often described as an insidious disease.
words.trap: با 'invidious' (نفرت‌انگیز) شباهت دارد اما insidious بیشتر برای خطرات پنهان

words.coreMeaning: داشتن قضاوت خوب و عاقلانه
definitions: Having, showing, or done with good judgment or sense.
Prudent; wise.
examples: A judicious use of resources can save the company money.
The judicious editor removed the unnecessary paragraphs.
words.trap: با 'judicial' (قضایی) اشتباه نگیرید؛ judicious یعنی خردمندانه، judicial یعنی مربوط به دادگاه

words.coreMeaning: شادی و سرور شدید
definitions: Feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph.
Exultant; overjoyed.
examples: The jubilant fans celebrated their team's championship victory.
She was jubilant when she received the acceptance letter.
words.trap: از لاتین jubilare (فریاد شادی)؛ با 'jubilee' (جشن سالگرد) مرتبط

words.coreMeaning: روشن کردن آتش یا برانگیختن احساس
definitions: To light or set on fire.
To arouse or inspire an emotion or reaction.
examples: Her words kindled a passion for learning in the students.
He kindled a fire in the fireplace to warm the room.
words.trap: با نام Kindle (کتابخوان آمازون) ارتباط ریشه‌ای دارد؛ هم معنای ظاهری و هم مجازی

words.coreMeaning: ارتباط خونی یا احساس نزدیکی
definitions: Blood relationship.
A sharing of characteristics or origins; a close connection.
examples: She felt a strong kinship with other survivors of the disaster.
The kinship between the two languages is evident in their vocabulary.
words.trap: از 'kin' (خویشاوند) + 'ship'؛ هم خونی و هم مجازی

words.coreMeaning: استفاده از کمترین کلمات ممکن
definitions: Using very few words; concise to the point of seeming rude.
Brief and to the point.
examples: His laconic reply — 'Fine' — did little to reassure her.
The laconic message simply read: 'Arrived safely.'
words.trap: از لاتین Laconia (لاکونیا، محل زندگی اسپارتی‌ها معروف به کم‌حرفی)

words.coreMeaning: ابازار غم و اندوه
definitions: To mourn a person's loss or death.
To express regret or disappointment over something considered unsatisfactory.
A passionate expression of grief.
examples: Citizens lamented the loss of green spaces in the city.
The poet wrote a lament for his fallen comrades.
His lament about the good old days bored everyone.
words.trap: هم فعل و هم اسم؛ lamentable به معنای 'تأسف‌بار' است

words.coreMeaning: فاقد انرژی و سرزندگی
definitions: Displaying a disinclination for physical exertion; slow and relaxed.
Weak or faint from illness or fatigue.
examples: She waved a languid hand in dismissal.
The languid summer afternoon made everyone sleepy.
words.trap: با 'language' (زبان) ارتباط ریشه‌ای ندارد؛ از لاتین languere

words.coreMeaning: وضوح ذهنی و قابل فهم بودن
definitions: Expressed clearly; easy to understand.
Bright or luminous.
Having full use of one's faculties; sane.
examples: Despite her illness, she remained lucid until the end.
The book provides a lucid explanation of quantum physics.
He had a lucid dream in which he could control his actions.
words.trap: از لاتین lux (نور)؛ 'lucid dream' (رؤیای شفاف) یک اصطلاح رایج است

words.coreMeaning: تولید سود و درآمد زیاد
definitions: Producing a great deal of profit.
Highly profitable.
examples: The tech industry offers many lucrative career opportunities.
Real estate can be a lucrative investment if done wisely.
words.trap: از لاتین lucrum (سود)؛ فرم قدیمی‌تر 'lucre' هنوز در 'filthy lucre' استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: دارای روح بزرگ و بخشندگی
definitions: Very generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person.
Noble in spirit; generous.
examples: The magnanimous winner congratulated his defeated opponent.
Her magnanimous gesture of forgiveness moved everyone.
words.trap: از لاتین magnus (بزرگ) + animus (ذهن)؛ با 'magnify' (بزرگ‌نمایی) اشتباه نگیرید

words.coreMeaning: قابل شکل‌دهی یا تأثیرپذیر
definitions: Easily influenced; pliable.
Capable of being shaped or bent.
examples: Young children's minds are highly malleable.
Gold is one of the most malleable metals.
words.trap: در فلزات: قابل چکش‌خواری؛ در روانشناسی: قابل تأثیر

words.coreMeaning: توجه بسیار زیاد به جزئیات
definitions: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
Excessively concerned with details.
examples: She is meticulous in her research, leaving no stone unturned.
The meticulous craftsmanship of the furniture was evident.
words.trap: از لاتین meticulosus (ترسو) اما امروزه به معنای دقیق استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: کاهش شدت یا جدیت چیزی
definitions: To make less severe, serious, or painful.
To lessen the gravity of an offense.
examples: Steps were taken to mitigate the effects of the drought.
The lawyer argued mitigating circumstances in favor of the defendant.
words.trap: با 'militate' (تأثیر منفی گذاشتن) اشتباه نگیرید؛ mitigate against غیراستاندارد است

words.trap: با bellicose اشتباه گرفته نشود؛ هر دو به معنای جنگ‌طلب هستند اما belligerent بیشتر برای توصیف رفتار فعلی استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: احترام و تبعیت فروتنانه در برابر دیگری
definitions: Humble respect and submission to another's judgment
A yielding to the opinion or wishes of another
examples: The young lawyer showed deference to the senior partner's experience.
Out of deference to her wishes, they changed the venue of the party.
words.trap: با difference اشتباه نشود؛ تلفظ و معنا کاملاً متفاوت است

words.coreMeaning: وضعیت بد را بدتر کردن یا شدت بخشیدن به مشکل
definitions: To make a problem or situation worse
To increase the severity of a disease or condition
examples: His careless remarks only exacerbated the already tense situation.
The drought was exacerbated by the lack of government intervention.
words.trap: با exaggerate اشتباه گرفته نشود؛ exacerbate یعنی بدتر کردن، exaggerate یعنی بزرگ‌نمایی

words.coreMeaning: بیش از حد حرف زدن؛ وراج و خسته‌کننده
definitions: Excessively talkative, especially about trivial things
Verbose and rambling in speech
examples: The garrulous taxi driver talked nonstop during the entire ride.
Her garrulous neighbor kept her on the phone for over an hour.
words.trap: با gorgeous اشتباه نشود؛ garrulous به معنای وراج است نه زیبا

words.coreMeaning: به حالت ضعف و ناتوانی افتادن؛ بدون پیشرفت ماندن
definitions: To lose vitality or strength; to become weak
To be forced to remain in an unpleasant situation for a long time
examples: The prisoners languished in jail for years without a trial.
The project languished due to lack of funding and interest.
words.trap: با language اشتباه نشود؛ languish فعل به معنای تضعیف شدن است

words.coreMeaning: بسیار بد و شرورانه؛ خلاف قانون و اخلاق
definitions: Wicked or criminal; extremely evil
Involving serious wrongdoing or criminal activity
examples: The police uncovered the criminal's nefarious plot to rob the bank.
His nefarious activities eventually caught up with him.
words.trap: با fabulous اشتباه نشود؛ nefarious به معنای شرورانه است نه افسانه‌ای

words.coreMeaning: بیش از حد مطیع و چاپلوس برای جلب رضایت دیگران
definitions: Excessively compliant or deferential; servile
Obedient or attentive to an excessive degree
examples: The obsequious waiter hovered over the table, anticipating every need.
His obsequious behavior toward the boss annoyed his coworkers.
words.trap: با obsolete اشتباه نشود؛ obsequious به معنای چاپلوس است نه منسوخ

words.translation: فراز و نشیب، تغییر و تحول
words.coreMeaning: تغییرات غیرمنتظره و نوسانات سرنوشت
definitions: A change of circumstances, typically unwelcome
The natural ups and downs of life or fortune
examples: The vicissitudes of life taught him to be resilient and adaptable.
She weathered the vicissitudes of the stock market with patience.
words.trap: معمولاً به صورت جمع (vicissitudes) استفاده می‌شود و به تغییرات نامطلوب اشاره دارد

words.coreMeaning: روح و فرهنگ غالب یک دوره تاریخی خاص
definitions: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history
The general intellectual, moral, and cultural climate of an era
examples: The music of the 1960s perfectly captured the zeitgeist of the era.
Understanding the zeitgeist helps explain why certain movements gain traction.
words.trap: واژه آلمانی است و به صورت zeɪtgaɪst تلفظ می‌شود نه زیت‌گیست

words.coreMeaning: عمداً از انجام کاری خودداری کردن
definitions: To restrain oneself from doing or enjoying something
To formally decline to vote on an issue
examples: The judge decided to abstain from the case due to a conflict of interest.
He chose to abstain from alcohol during the month of Ramadan.
words.trap: همیشه با from استفاده می‌شود: abstain from something

words.coreMeaning: آسان برای دسترسی، فهم یا استفاده
definitions: Easy to approach, reach, or understand
Available to people with disabilities; inclusive
examples: The professor made complex topics accessible to beginners.
The new building is fully accessible to wheelchair users.
words.trap: با access (دسترسی) ارتباط دارد اما accessible صفت است و معانی گسترده‌تری دارد

words.coreMeaning: شرایط سخت و دشوار زندگی؛ بدبختی و مصیبت
definitions: A difficult or unpleasant situation or condition
Misfortune or hardship
examples: She showed great courage in the face of adversity.
Adversity builds character and tests one's resilience.
words.trap: معمولاً به صورت جمع (adversities) هم استفاده می‌شود؛ ضرب‌المثل: Adversity builds character

words.coreMeaning: بسیار سخت و نیازمند تلاش زیاد
definitions: Involving or requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring
Hard to climb or traverse
examples: The arduous journey through the mountains took three days.
Learning a new language is an arduous but rewarding process.
words.trap: با hard تفاوت دارد؛ arduous رسمی‌تر و شدیدتر است

words.coreMeaning: توانایی صحبت کردن واضح و مؤثر
definitions: Having or showing the ability to speak fluently and coherently
To express an idea fluently and coherently
examples: She is an articulate speaker who can explain complex ideas simply.
He struggled to articulate his feelings about the situation.
words.trap: هم صفت (فصیح) و هم فعل (بیان کردن) است

words.coreMeaning: تلاش مداوم و دقیق در انجام کار
definitions: Showing great care and perseverance
Diligent and persistent in effort
examples: The assiduous student studied every night to maintain her grades.
His assiduous attention to detail ensured the project's success.
words.trap: با assiduous (پرتلاش) و assiduously (با پشتکار) ارتباط دارد

words.coreMeaning: احساس رضایت خطرناک از خود بدون توجه به خطرات
definitions: Showing smug or uncritical satisfaction with oneself
Self-satisfied to the point of neglecting potential dangers
examples: The team became complacent after their early success and lost the championship.
Don't be complacent about your health—get regular check-ups.
words.trap: با compliant (مطیع) اشتباه نشود؛ complacent منفی و compliant خنثی است

words.coreMeaning: قبول یا نادیده گرفتن رفتار نادرست
definitions: To accept and allow behavior that is considered wrong to continue
To overlook or forgive an offense
examples: The school cannot condone cheating under any circumstances.
By staying silent, she seemed to condone his inappropriate behavior.
words.trap: با condemn (محکوم کردن) کاملاً متضاد است

words.coreMeaning: جلب توجه کردن به دلیل برجسته بودن
definitions: Standing out so as to be clearly visible; attracting notice
Noticeable or remarkable
examples: Her bright red coat made her conspicuous in the crowd.
His absence from the meeting was conspicuous and raised questions.
words.trap: ضرب‌المثل: Conspicuous by its absence (با غیابش برجسته شد)

words.coreMeaning: احساس بی‌ارزشی و تحقیر نسبت به کسی یا چیزی
definitions: The feeling that a person or thing is beneath consideration or worthless
Open disrespect or willful disobedience of a court
examples: She looked at the messy room with contempt.
The judge held the witness in contempt of court.
words.trap: contemptible = قابل تحقیر، contemptuous = تحقیرآمیز

words.coreMeaning: آسان فریب خوردن؛ بدون شک و تردید
definitions: Having or showing too great a readiness to believe things
Easily deceived; gullible
examples: The credulous audience believed every word the con artist said.
Don't be so credulous—not every advertisement tells the truth.
words.trap: با credible (معتبر) اشتباه نشود؛ credulous منفی و credible مثبت است

words.coreMeaning: انجام کار به شکل سریع و بدون دقت کافی
definitions: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed
Done rapidly without attention to details
examples: A cursory glance at the report revealed several errors.
The cursory inspection failed to detect the hidden defects.
words.trap: با cursor (نشانگر) اشتباه نشود؛ cursory به معنای سطحی و سرسری است

words.coreMeaning: رفتار مودبانه و مناسب در اجتماع
definitions: Behavior in keeping with good taste and propriety; politeness
Dignified and appropriate conduct
examples: The guests maintained proper decorum throughout the formal dinner.
Students are expected to show decorum during the ceremony.
words.trap: با decoration (تزیین) اشتباه نشود؛ decorum به معنای نزاکت و ادب است

words.coreMeaning: احساس ناامیدی و دلسردی شدید
definitions: In low spirits from loss of hope or courage
Feeling a profound discouragement and hopelessness
examples: She became despondent after receiving multiple rejection letters.
The despondent team had lost all hope of winning the tournament.
words.trap: با desperate (مأیوس) تفاوت دارد؛ despondent آرام‌تر و غمگین‌تر از desperate است

words.coreMeaning: دور شدن از موضوع اصلی در صحبت یا نوشتن
definitions: To leave the main subject temporarily in speech or writing
To deviate from the main topic
examples: The professor tends to digress during lectures, sharing personal anecdotes.
Let me digress for a moment to tell you a related story.
words.trap: با regress (عقب‌گرد) و progress (پیشرفت) خانواده لغوی دارد

words.coreMeaning: از تعادل خارج کردن؛ گیج و ناراحت کردن
definitions: To disturb the composure of; to unsettle
To make someone feel confused and slightly worried
examples: His unexpected question disconcerted the speaker.
The strange noise disconcerted the sleeping children.
words.trap: با disconnect (قطع کردن) اشتباه نشود؛ disconcert به معنای گیج کردن است

words.coreMeaning: تفاوت بزرگ و ناعادلانه بین دو چیز
definitions: A great difference or inequality
An instance of difference or inequality
examples: The disparity between the rich and the poor continues to grow.
There is a significant disparity in pay between men and women.
words.trap: با disparity (نابرابری) و disparity (بدشکلی) اشتباه نشود

words.coreMeaning: خوش‌اخلاق و مهربان در رفتار
definitions: Having a friendly and pleasant manner
Good-natured and likable
examples: The amiable professor was beloved by all his students.
Her amiable personality made her popular at work.
words.trap: با amicable (دوستانه) تفاوت دارد؛ amiable برای افراد و amicable برای روابط

words.coreMeaning: داشتن احساسات متناقض درباره چیزی
definitions: Having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something.
Uncertain or indecisive about something.
examples: She felt ambivalent about accepting the job offer.
His ambivalent attitude confused his colleagues.
words.trap: با 'ambiguous' (مبهم) فرق دارد؛ ambivalent مربوط به احساسات است

words.coreMeaning: بازگشت به ویژگی‌های اجدادی
definitions: Reversion to an earlier type; a recurrence of a past characteristic.
A tendency to revert to ancestral traits.
examples: His violent outburst was seen as a form of atavism.
The atavism of certain behaviors puzzled the researchers.
words.trap: با 'avatar' (آواتار) اشتباه نگیرید

words.coreMeaning: بهتر کردن وضعیت یا شرایط نامطلوب
definitions: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better
To improve or make more bearable
examples: The new policy was designed to ameliorate the living conditions of the poor.
Steps were taken to ameliorate the effects of the drought on farmers.
words.trap: با improve تفاوت رسمیت دارد؛ ameliorate رسمی‌تر است و بیشتر در متون آکادمیک استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: شوخی کردن در موقعیت‌های جدی و نابجا
definitions: Treating serious issues with inappropriate humor
Trying to be amusing at an inappropriate time
examples: His facetious remarks during the serious meeting annoyed the manager.
She made a facetious comment about the accident, which shocked everyone.
words.trap: با factitious اشتباه نشود؛ facetious به معنای شوخی نابجا است و factitious به معنای مصنوعی

words.coreMeaning: کسی که باورها و سنت‌های پذیرفته شده را به چالش می‌کشد
definitions: A person who attacks or criticizes cherished beliefs or institutions
Someone who challenges established traditions or norms
examples: As an iconoclast, she questioned every tradition the company held dear.
The artist was an iconoclast who rejected conventional artistic standards.
words.trap: ریشه یونانی دارد: eikon (تصویر) + klastes (شکننده)؛ با icon (نماد) ارتباط ریشه‌ای دارد اما معنا متفاوت است

words.coreMeaning: ملی‌گرایی افراطی و تهاجمی؛ حمایت بی‌قید و شرط از سیاست‌های جنگ‌طلبانه
definitions: Extreme patriotism, especially in the form of aggressive foreign policy
Nationalistic and bellicose chauvinism
examples: The politician's jingoism appealed to voters who wanted a strong military stance.
Jingoism often leads to conflicts with other nations.
words.trap: با patriotism تفاوت دارد؛ jingoism بار منفی دارد و به ملی‌گرایی افراطی و تهاجمی اشاره می‌کند

words.coreMeaning: به طور مبالغه‌آمیز احترام گذاشتن یا اطاعت کردن
definitions: To act in an excessively submissive or deferential manner
To show excessive respect or obedience
examples: She refused to kowtow to her boss's unreasonable demands.
The employees were expected to kowtow to the company's authoritarian CEO.
words.trap: ریشه چینی دارد (叩頭) و به معنای تعظیم زمینی در فرهنگ چینی است؛ در انگلیسی بار منفی دارد

words.coreMeaning: تمایل زیاد به حرف زدن؛ خوش‌صحبت اما گاهی بیش از حد
definitions: Tending to talk a great deal; talkative
Full of excessive conversation
examples: The loquacious host kept the guests entertained with stories all evening.
My loquacious aunt can talk for hours without pausing.
words.trap: با eloquent تفاوت دارد؛ loquacious فقط به معنای پرحرف بودن است اما eloquent به معنای خوب صحبت کردن

words.coreMeaning: فاقد ویژگی‌های خاص یا جالب توجه؛ خسته‌کننده و معمولی
definitions: Lacking distinctive or interesting features; dull
Not easily classified or described; unremarkable
examples: The nondescript building blended into the gray cityscape.
He wore a nondescript outfit that attracted no attention whatsoever.
words.trap: با non-descriptive اشتباه نشود؛ nondescript یک کلمه واحد است و به معنای بی‌خاصیت

words.coreMeaning: عمداً مبهم یا گیج‌کننده کردن چیزی
definitions: To render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible
To deliberately make something confusing or difficult to understand
examples: The politician tried to obfuscate the issue with complex statistics.
Legal jargon often obfuscates the meaning of contracts for ordinary people.
words.trap: با obscure تفاوت دارد؛ obfuscate عمدی و عامدانه است اما obscure ممکن است طبیعی باشد

words.coreMeaning: بیش از حد صرفه‌جو و خسیس بودن در خرج کردن
definitions: Excessively unwilling to spend money or use resources
Extremely frugal; miserly
examples: The parsimonious millionaire refused to donate a single penny to charity.
His parsimonious habits meant he rarely treated his friends to dinner.
words.trap: با frugal تفاوت دارد؛ parsimonious بار منفی دارد (خسیس) اما frugal مثبت (صرفه‌جو)

words.coreMeaning: کسی که برای منفعت شخصی چاپلوسی می‌کند
definitions: A person who acts obsequiously toward someone to gain advantage
A self-seeking flatterer
examples: The king was surrounded by sycophants who praised his every decision.
She saw through the sycophant's flattery and dismissed him immediately.
words.trap: با SYCO اشتباه نشود؛ sycophant شخصی است که برای منفعت چاپلوسی می‌کند

words.coreMeaning: توجه به نفع دیگران بدون انتظار پاداش
definitions: Showing a selfless concern for the well-being of others
Unselfish and generous in spirit
examples: Her altruistic donation helped build a school in the rural village.
The altruistic volunteer dedicated her weekends to helping the homeless.
words.trap: با altruism (نوع‌دوستی) ارتباط دارد و هر دو از egoism (خودپرستی) متضاد هستند

words.coreMeaning: احساس شدید دشمنی و بدخواهی نسبت به دیگری
definitions: Strong hostility or active hatred
A deep-seated feeling of ill will or enmity
examples: There was a long-standing animosity between the two rival families.
The animosity between the political parties made compromise impossible.
words.trap: با animal (حیوان) اشتباه نشود؛ animosity به معنای خصومت و دشمنی شدید است

words.coreMeaning: آرام کردن خشم یا نگرانی با امتیاز دادن
definitions: To pacify or satisfy by granting concessions
To bring peace or calm to a troubled situation
examples: The government tried to appease the protesters by promising reforms.
She offered food to appease the crying child.
words.trap: بار منفی دارد وقتی به معنای امتیاز دادن بیش از حد باشد؛ مثلاً سیاست مماشات هیتلر

words.coreMeaning: داشتن قدرت درک و تحلیل سریع و دقیق
definitions: Having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations and turn them to one's advantage
Sharp and perceptive in judgment
examples: The astute investor recognized the opportunity before anyone else.
Her astute observations about human nature made her a great novelist.
words.trap: با astute (زیرک) و acute (حاد) تفاوت دارد؛ astute بیشتر برای هوش و زیرکی استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: ساده و بدون تجمل؛ سخت‌گیرانه و جدی
definitions: Severe or strict in manner or appearance
Having no comforts or luxuries; very simple
examples: The monks lived an austere life, with few possessions and simple food.
The austere classroom had only desks, chairs, and a blackboard.
words.trap: با austerely (سخت‌گیرانه) و austerity (ریاضت) ارتباط دارد؛ در اقتصاد به معنای سیاست ریاضتی هم است

words.coreMeaning: خجالت کشیدن و کم‌رو بودن در حضور دیگران
definitions: Reluctant to draw attention to oneself; shy
Timid and easily embarrassed
examples: The bashful child hid behind her mother when meeting strangers.
He was too bashful to ask her to dance at the prom.
words.trap: با bash (کوبیدن) اشتباه نشود؛ bashful به معنای خجالتی و کم‌رو است

words.coreMeaning: بی‌ضرر و مهربان؛ خوش‌خیم (در پزشکی)
definitions: Gentle and kindly; not harmful or malignant
Of a tumor or growth: not cancerous
examples: The doctor confirmed that the tumor was benign and posed no threat.
Her benign smile put the nervous visitors at ease.
words.trap: با malignant (بدخیم) متضاد است؛ در پزشکی benign tumor یعنی تومور خوش‌خیم

words.coreMeaning: بی‌خیال و بی‌توجه نسبت به مشکلات؛ شاد و سبک‌سر
definitions: Showing a casual and cheerful indifference; carefree
Happy and lighthearted
examples: She had a blithe disregard for the rules that frustrated her teachers.
The blithe melody of the song lifted everyone's spirits.
words.trap: با blight (آفت) اشتباه نشود؛ blithe به معنای بی‌خیال و شاد است

words.coreMeaning: بیان نادرست و بدخواهانه برای آسیب رساندن به شهرت کسی
definitions: The making of false and defamatory statements to damage someone's reputation
A false and malicious statement designed to injure
examples: The politician was a victim of calumny spread by his opponents.
She sued the newspaper for publishing calumny against her.
words.trap: با calumniate (افترا زدن) و calumnious (افترا‌آمیز) ارتباط دارد

words.coreMeaning: سرزنش و تنبیه شدید کسی برای اشتباه
definitions: To reprimand someone severely
To criticize or punish harshly
examples: The teacher castigated the student for cheating on the exam.
The media castigated the politician for breaking his campaign promises.
words.trap: با chastise (تنبیه کردن) شباهت دارد اما castigate شدیدتر و رسمی‌تر است

words.coreMeaning: ثبت و ضبط وقایع به ترتیب زمانی
definitions: A factual written account of important historical events in order of their occurrence
To record events in a factual and detailed way
examples: The book chronicles the rise and fall of the ancient empire.
She chronicled her travel experiences in a detailed journal.
words.trap: با chronic (مزمن) اشتباه نشود؛ chronicle به معنای ثبت وقایع است و chronic به معنای مزمن

words.coreMeaning: پایان یافتن یا متوقف شدن کامل
definitions: The fact or process of ending or being brought to an end
A pause or cessation of activity
examples: The cessation of hostilities brought relief to the war-torn region.
After the cessation of rain, the sun appeared.
words.trap: با session (جلسه) اشتباه نشود

words.coreMeaning: متناسب و هماهنگ با چیز دیگر
definitions: Corresponding in size or degree; in proportion
Proportionate to something
examples: The salary should be commensurate with experience.
The punishment was commensurate with the crime.
words.trap: با communicate (ارتباط برقرار کردن) اشتباه نشود

words.coreMeaning: وادار کردن کسی به انجام کار
definitions: To force someone to do something; to oblige
To evoke a strong reaction or feeling
examples: The evidence compelled the jury to reach a guilty verdict.
Her performance compelled the audience to give a standing ovation.
words.trap: معمولاً به شکل feel compelled (احساس اجبار کردن) استفاده می‌شود

words.coreMeaning: احساس رضایت و خشنودی از وضعیت موجود
definitions: A state of happiness and satisfaction
Peace of mind and contentment
examples: She found contentment in the simple pleasures of life.
True contentment comes from within, not from material possessions.
words.trap: با content (محتوا) تفاوت دارد؛ contentment به معنای رضایت است

words.coreMeaning: نقص یا عیب ظاهری
definitions: A flaw or defect that spoils appearance
To spoil the appearance or quality of
examples: The diamond had a tiny blemish that reduced its value.
His perfect record was blemished by one mistake.
words.trap: با embellish (تزیین کردن) اشتباه نشود

words.coreMeaning: داشتن استدلال قوی و قانع‌کننده
definitions: Clear, logical, and convincing; compelling
Appealing forcibly to the mind or reason
examples: The lawyer presented a cogent argument that swayed the jury.
Her cogent reasoning left no room for doubt.
words.trap: با cognate (هم‌خانواده) اشتباه نشود

words.coreMeaning: داشتن اثر مضر و آسیب‌رسان
definitions: Causing harm or damage; harmful
Tending to cause harm
examples: Smoking is detrimental to health.
The detrimental effects of pollution are well documented.
words.trap: با deleterious (مضر) شباهت دارد اما detrimental رایج‌تر است

words.coreMeaning: محتاط و دوراندیش بودن قبل از اقدام
definitions: Wary and unwilling to take risks; prudent
Careful to consider all circumstances before acting
examples: The circumspect lawyer reviewed every detail of the contract.
A circumspect approach to investing can protect against major losses.
